prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: production 2.5D survival game character WALK CYCLE sprite atlas with genuine transparent alpha.
Reference image: the attached existing eight-direction Patch robot atlas is the exact character identity and rendering style to retain. Create a NEW animation sheet, not a collage of the original static poses.

Primary request: a precisely organized square 2048 by 2048 PNG sprite atlas, exactly 8 columns by 8 rows, 64 separate full-body sprites, every cell 256 by 256 pixels. Each row is one direction; every column is a successive distinct phase of one smooth looping eight-frame bipedal walk. No border, labels, text, arrows, floor or background.

Character: Patch (P-04), the same squat friendly battered rescue robot in the reference: heavy rounded riveted oxidized olive/bronze/cream metal chassis, small amber visor eye, cream downward rescue chevrons on chest, orange repair plate, caged amber beacon on top, articulated short mechanical legs with two broad separate metal feet, articulated arms, winch coil, worn brown canvas satchel, clipped receiver wires. Preserve anatomy, proportions, accessories and viewpoint consistently. Faithful detailed hand-painted isometric game art with crisp silhouettes and clearly separated feet; strengthen pale metal highlights and readable amber eye subtly without redesigning him.

GRID AND CAMERA: use exactly the same fixed elevated three-quarter game camera as the reference. 8 rows from top to bottom:
row 1 faces screen DOWN, looking toward camera.
row 2 faces DOWN-RIGHT, three-quarter front, walking toward bottom-right.
row 3 faces RIGHT, true right-facing side view.
row 4 faces UP-RIGHT, three-quarter back walking toward top-right.
row 5 faces UP, complete back view.
row 6 faces UP-LEFT, three-quarter back walking toward top-left.
row 7 faces LEFT, true left-facing side view.
row 8 faces DOWN-LEFT, three-quarter front walking toward bottom-left.
In each row, keep that EXACT facing in all eight frames; never rotate within a row. Render opposite directions from actual matching views, not mirrored labels/accessories.

GAIT: all eight columns are visibly different leg and arm poses, not repeated idle sprites and not a rigid body tilted sideways.
Columns 1 to 8: left heel contact, left planted/right toe pushing off, right leg passing the planted left leg, right knee lifting/forward swing, right heel contact, right planted/left toe pushing off, left leg passing the planted right leg, left knee lifting/forward swing. Alternate the arms opposite the legs. A sturdy slightly weighted mechanical gait with real hip/knee/ankle articulation, clear planted-versus-lifted foot, small natural satchel follow-through. Both legs must always remain identifiable. Frame 8 flows naturally into frame 1.

REGISTRATION: in EVERY cell, keep the same body size, chassis center and camera framing. Robot from beacon top to planted foot is approximately 200 pixels high, head around y=28, central ground anchor at x=128,y=228 relative to each cell. Allow slight natural body rise/fall, but NEVER resize a frame. Keep the whole body and every hand/foot inside its own cell with at least 12 pixels of transparent clearance. No translated character traveling across the sheet. Do not crop any part. No cast shadows baked into sprites, no glow haze outside the beacon, no extra props.

OUTPUT: one clean 8 by 8 atlas on a truly transparent background with exactly 64 individually separated sprites. Preserve consistent paint detail and strong readable silhouettes. This will be shown at 90 pixels character height in game, so clear walking silhouettes and consistent feet are more important than tiny surface scratches.
